title: Phase transitions
objectives: Name and distinguish six phase transitions; identify energy absorbed or released; explain evaporation, boiling and condensation using particles.
difficulty: Beginner through application; final question is a challenge
instructions: Show the equation, substitution, arithmetic and units for numerical answers. Explain physical meaning. Use given constants. Retain intermediate digits and round final answers as requested; for unspecified precision, accept sensible rounding. Graphs and data are simulated educational models.

questions.prompt: For the sample undergoing the transition, which absorbs heat: melting or freezing? State what the other process does.
A wet towel dries at 24 °C. Must its water have boiled? Name the applicable process.
A 75.0 g sealed sample of ice is partly melted. There are 27.0 g of liquid water. Find the remaining ice mass and percentage melted.
Water vapor forms liquid droplets on a cooler surface. Name the transition, identify the energy direction for the vapor becoming liquid, and state whether H₂O becomes a new chemical substance.
During one modeled interval, 9.0 g evaporates and 4.0 g condenses inside a closed container. Find the net liquid-mass change and explain what happens to total mass.
Challenge: A student labels a frost crystal forming directly from water vapor “freezing” and says it absorbs heat. Correct both claims and explain the particle change.
